svg.title: Senior Transition Sale Roadmap
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-senior-transition-roadmap; chapter number: 12; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Senior Transition Sale Roadmap; subtitle: Authority first, then the house, then the capital; caption: Sheri Coleman reports as short as 6 weeks from family meeting to closing once a power of attorney and a single family contact are in place.; assumptions note: The four weeks are a sequencing frame, not a reported duration; actual timing depends on asking price and finding the right buyer.; note: Sequence per Florida Realtors YouTube, Dale Corpus, The Cobb Home Team, Ariana Jay, Brett Chotkevys, Serg Lupescu, and Unit Math.; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Lock legal authority; deliverable: Power of attorney or the senior signing, plus one designated family contact.; gate: No senior listing without both.; week: Week 2; title: Payoff and pricing; deliverable: Reverse mortgage balance confirmed, since it is paid off at closing; family educated on current market conditions.; gate: No overpriced list that stalls and frustrates the family.; week: Week 3; title: Fund the care; deliverable: Bay Area assisted living or memory care at $5,000 to $12,000-plus per month, often funded by the home sale.; gate: Two years of private pay saved, with financial and medical POA and a will or trust.; week: Week 4; title: Redeploy capital; deliverable: Residential assisted living targets $3,000 to $10,000 per client per month; a $240 rough site plan clears zoning questions.; gate: Zoning confirmed for the exact address and debt service coverage near 1.2.
